decisive_items: Detection of a heterozygous pathogenic KRIT1 variant
The patient used a wheelchair due to right-sided hemiparesis and hemianopsia caused by an intracranial hemorrhage
Family history revealed similar conditions in the patient's father and aunt, with the father having died of an intracranial hemorrhage in his early 70s
response.rationale: KRIT1 pathogenic variant, intracranial hemorrhage, and autosomal dominant family history are diagnostic of cerebral cavernous malformation; skin lesions are consistent cutaneous manifestations. Lipolymphedema is a secondary finding, not the primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Lipolymphedema is a comorbid condition attributed to venous insufficiency, not the unifying diagnosis given KRIT1 and hemorrhage history.
Cutaneovisceral angiomatosis with thrombocytopenia lacks thrombocytopenia and visceral involvement; KRIT1 variant is not associated with this entity.
